purpose: How a tax preparation practice converts one season's finished returns into a returning client base and a year-round revenue shape: what actually makes a client come back and how that is measured honestly, what is captured and said in the weeks after the deadline, which off-season lines the practice is authorized and competent to run, how those commitments are fitted to a calendar that must still protect recovery, preparation and peak, and how referral-led growth is paced so it is never paid for out of the service level that holds the existing book.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all scores are heuristic priors
the practice is small enough that the owner personally knows most of the book and can recall a client's season without a report, which is exactly why the book must still be written down

retention rates, fee levels, off-season revenue shares, referral conversion and any practice or client-base valuation are treated as mechanisms and as the practice's own measured history, never as imported industry figures

credential and registration classes, consent-and-disclosure rules governing use of taxpayer data, compensated-referral permissions and record retention periods are jurisdiction- and credential-specific obligation classes that must be verified against the authority's current publications each cycle

the practice's year has one dominant filing peak with an extended-filing tail; a practice whose jurisdiction or client mix produces a different calendar shape must re-map the capacity blocks before using the smoothing logic
exclusions: preparer credential and registration classes, electronic-filing authorization, preparation-software and systems selection, the choice of client segment and service model, the seasonal demand curve as an economic mechanism, peak-capacity modelling, published intake cutoff policy and the per-return pricing architecture: the practice-setup sibling knowledge base owns all of these and this knowledge base consumes them only as fixed constraints

the per-return production pipeline from intake through document collection, preparation, review, signature and transmission, the named error classes and their controls, the per-return due-diligence documentation record, the in-return research-escalate-decline decision on an ambiguous item, and the security controls protecting taxpayer data at rest and in transit: the return-workflow sibling knowledge base owns all of these

correcting the practice's own filing errors: disclosure, an amendment filed as remediation, and any authority notice traceable to the practice's own work stay inside the return-workflow knowledge base's correction path and are never repriced or marketed as an off-season revenue line

tax advice, positions or conclusions on any specific taxpayer's facts; this knowledge base is practice and process knowledge and is educational rather than personalized tax, legal, financial or investment advice

any promise, implication or comparison about refund size or refund speed, any fee that varies with a refund amount or with an amount recovered on an amendment, any use of audit, penalty or notice fear as a selling lever, and any off-season pressure applied to elderly, bereaved, financially distressed or language-barriered clients

treating due-diligence obligations on credits and filing statuses as negotiable: they are compliance classes to respect, and this knowledge base never relaxes them for a valued client, a referral source or a high-contribution tier

invented retention percentages, churn benchmarks, competitor fee tables, off-season revenue shares, referral conversion rates, market sizes, practice valuations or client-base multiples presented as fact

current statutory specifics such as extension and estimated-payment dates, payment obligations, penalty amounts, consent-form wording requirements, compensated-referral permissions and record retention periods, all of which change between seasons and must be read from the authority's own current publications for the practice's jurisdiction

representation before a tax authority beyond what the practice's credential class permits, legal opinions, attest and audit engagements, and the performance of bookkeeping work itself as opposed to the decision whether to offer it

competency_questions.question: What exactly counts as a client who came back, and how is the practice's retention computed so that two people pulling the list get the same number?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RETURNING_BOOK_DEFINITION fixes the counting unit, the linked-group rule, the returned event and the active/lapsed/exited states, and RETENTION_MEASUREMENT supplies a dated cohort denominator and numerator with the post-extension recompute

competency_questions.question: Why do clients actually come back, and how do I tell earned loyalty apart from inertia before the inertia breaks?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RETENTION_MECHANISM_MAP names the retention forces with the behaviours that produce each and the signals that read them, and CHURN_REASON_CAPTURE supplies the exit evidence that corrects the reading

competency_questions.question: In the two weeks after the deadline, what must I write down and what must I say to each client before the season fades?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: POST_SEASON_DEBRIEF_WINDOW lists the per-client and per-practice facts to capture in a scheduled block, and NEXT_YEAR_POSITIONING states what each client is told about next season and on what grounds

competency_questions.question: How often may I contact my clients between seasons, about what, and what am I never allowed to say or imply?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FOLLOWUP_CONTACT_SEQUENCE gives the cadence and the one-ask rule, OFFSEASON_CONDUCT_BOUNDARY gives the never-say list and the vulnerable-client care rule, and CLIENT_CONTACT_CONSENT_AND_DATA_USE gives the permitted-use obligation class with its verify-current-rules requirement

competency_questions.question: A client emails a detailed question about their own situation in July and expects an answer because they are a client: what do I do with it?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: EDUCATION_VS_ADVICE_LINE classifies the request as general, fact-specific or outside competence and states the no-casual-answer habit and the conversion path, and PLANNING_ADJACENT_EDUCATION shows what may be said generally instead

competency_questions.question: Which off-season services am I actually permitted and competent to offer, and how do I decide before I promise anything to a client?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: OFFSEASON_SERVICE_ELIGIBILITY_FILTER states the authorization, competence, infrastructure and capacity test with an offer/refer/defer verdict and the verify-current-rules requirement, and BOOKKEEPING_CROSSOVER_LINE shows the test applied to the hardest candidate line

competency_questions.question: How do I run the extension population through the quiet months without building a second crunch at the extended deadline?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: EXTENSION_BOOK_MANAGEMENT supplies the tracked list, the per-client next action and governing date, the wave sequencing and the structural-versus-behavioural conversion test, and CAPACITY_SMOOTHING_PLAN places the waves in a named block

competency_questions.question: When is an amendment a service I sell, and when is it something I fix at my own cost?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: AMENDMENT_SERVICE_LINE limits the line to externally-originated situations with per-engagement scope, fee and review and bars outcome-promising review offers, and NOTICE_SUPPORT_LINE supplies the check-my-own-file-first rule that routes own-error matters out of the revenue lines

competency_questions.question: A client forwards an authority notice in August: what is the service, where does it stop, and how fast must it move?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: NOTICE_SUPPORT_LINE defines triage, deadline identification, file retrieval, documented response support, the same-week intake rule and the referral point, and OFFSEASON_SERVICE_ELIGIBILITY_FILTER supplies the authorization boundary that decides whether the practice may act at all

competency_questions.question: How do I build recurring revenue in the quiet months without spending the recovery and preparation time that the next peak depends on?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CAPACITY_SMOOTHING_PLAN names the year blocks, their protection rules and the refusal rule, and ESTIMATE_CYCLE_SERVICE shows a recurring line sized and dated against those blocks

competency_questions.question: Where do good new clients actually come from, how do I ask for them without pressure, and how many can I take this season?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: REFERRAL_GENERATION_MECHANISM describes the referrable moment, the single plain ask, source recording and the permitted-arrangement check, and BOOK_GROWTH_PACING derives the season's growth room from capacity minus expected returning demand

competency_questions.question: Which clients should I not carry into next season, and how do I decide who gets my scarce off-season attention?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CLIENT_DISENGAGEMENT_DECISION lists the practice-standard grounds, the early written notification and the document handover, and BOOK_VALUE_TIERING supplies the effort-adjusted contribution ranking that allocates attention without touching accuracy or refund size

competency_questions.question: What do I review once a year about the book itself, and what decisions must come out of it before the next season starts?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BOOK_HEALTH_REVIEW assembles retention, churn, line performance and mix evidence into a written decision set with owners and dates placed before the pre-season block, and RETENTION_MEASUREMENT supplies the dated figures it reads

glossary.definition: The set of households and small businesses that have filed with the practice and may choose to come back; between seasons it is the practice's principal asset, and unlike a subscription it renews only by an unforced annual decision on the client's side.

A client who skipped one season without a known exit event; distinct from an exited client because a meaningful share of lapsed clients file again, so counting them as churn understates retention and counting them as active overstates it.

The share of a given entry-year group that reached accepted transmission again in the current season, always stated with an as-of date and recomputed after the extended filing deadline so the late-filing tail is not read as churn.

The population of clients whose returns went on extension, held as a tracked list with a per-client next action, owner and governing date, and worked in waves through the quiet months rather than at the extended deadline.

A revenue-producing service the practice runs outside the filing peak: completing extension returns, externally-originated amendments, authority-notice support, recurring estimate cycles, general educational offers and bookkeeping crossover.

A named span of the practice's year - peak, recovery, working off-season, pre-season - to which every off-season commitment is assigned and against which commitments that would land in a protected block are refused, capped or rescheduled.

The point at which a client has just experienced something specific enough to repeat in one sentence to someone with a similar situation; referrals run on this moment, which is why the ask belongs at delivery rather than in a later campaign.

A client's fee measured against the hours the relationship truly consumes including document chase, mid-season scope changes, post-filing questions and payment follow-up; the only honest basis for tiering, and one that never includes refund size.

The practice's deliberate decision not to carry a client into the next season, taken on practice-standard grounds, notified in writing well before intake opens, and accompanied by an offer to hand over prior-year documents.

The explicit label attached to every educational piece and general answer stating that it is general information rather than advice on any individual's facts, paired with a date and the authority publication the content was checked against.

source_registry.description: heuristic prior estimates for returning_client_base_and_offseason_revenue work units in absence of supplied datasets
source_registry.citation_or_locator: heuristic prior; no external dataset supplied

nodes.definition: Fix what the practice actually owns between seasons: not a contract but a book of households and small businesses that each make a fresh, unforced decision every year about whether to come back. This work unit pins the counting unit (the filing client, with a jointly filing couple counted once and a business return plus its owners' personal returns held as one linked group), the event that counts as a return (accepted transmission, never an inquiry, an appointment or a signed organizer), and the states a client can be in: active, lapsed after a skipped season with no known exit, or exited because they died, moved to a filing situation the practice does not serve, or were deliberately disengaged. Everything downstream - retention measurement, off-season targeting, tiering, capacity planning - is unusable until these are pinned, because the same raw client list produces wildly different pictures under different unspoken definitions, and the practice ends up arguing about whether it is shrinking instead of deciding what to do.

included: the client counting unit and the linked-group rule for business plus owner returns
the accepted-transmission definition of a return event
active, lapsed and exited client states with the evidence each requires
the book framed as an asset that renews only by client decision
excluded: choosing which client segment the practice serves in the first place
constructing or changing the fee for a return
the per-return production work itself

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a new return type or entity class enters the practice, or a software migration changes what the client list contains

pros.claim: A pinned counting unit makes seasons comparable instead of drifting with whoever pulls the list
pros.example: counting a married couple filing jointly as one returning unit, so a year in which more couples file separately does not read as growth

pros.claim: Separating lapsed from exited stops the practice from writing off clients who routinely return after a gap
pros.example: a client who skipped the season their income fell below their filing requirement and files again the next year

cons.claim: Any fixed unit definition mishandles real family and entity shapes and forces manual adjudication
cons.example: a client whose business return stays with the practice while the personal return moves to a family member's preparer sits half in and half out of the book

failure_modes: counting inquiries, appointments or signed organizers as returns so the rate flatters the practice
letting the preparation software's client list stand in for the book, so a purge or a duplicate merge silently changes the denominator
treating every one-season gap as permanent churn and never contacting the client again
acceptance_tests: the written definition names the counting unit, the linked-group rule, the returned event and the three client states, and a second person recomputing the prior season's list from it reaches the same count
revisit_triggers: the practice starts accepting a return type or entity class the counting unit does not describe
the client list is migrated, merged or de-duplicated in the software
an adjudicated edge shape recurs often enough to need its own rule

nodes.definition: Build the practice's explicit account of why a given client returns, separating four forces that look identical inside a single retention number. Earned trust: the client believes the return was done correctly and that they were told the truth about it, including the parts they did not want to hear. Experienced ease: intake was painless, the questions were few and specific, answers came back quickly, and nothing had to be explained twice. Proactivity: the preparer raised something the client would never have thought to ask about and did it before it mattered. Inertia: prior-year data lives here, the preparer knows the family, and re-explaining a life to a stranger is exhausting. The map matters because inertia-held clients look perfectly retained right up to the season they are not, while trust-held and ease-held clients survive a fee increase, a moved appointment or a bad year. Each force is written with the concrete practice behaviours that produce it and the observable signal - response latency, repeated questions, unsolicited referrals, silence - that reads whether it is present.

included: the named retention forces and the practice behaviours that produce each
the observable signals that read which force is holding a given client
the fragility ranking that says which forces survive a fee change or a mistake
excluded: the per-return production behaviours themselves, which the return-workflow knowledge base owns
computing the aggregate retention rate
acquiring clients who have never filed with the practice

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: exit-reason evidence or a competitor's switching-cost move contradicts the force the map assigned to a client group

pros.claim: A named mechanism turns retention from a mood into something the practice can deliberately build and check
pros.example: recognising that a client stayed only because the prior-year data lives here, which means a competitor's free-transfer offer removes the entire reason they stayed

cons.claim: Attributing a client to a force is an inference from thin signals and can be confidently wrong
cons.example: reading a quiet client's silence as satisfaction when it is disengagement that ends the season the fee note arrives

cons.claim: The map invites the practice to credit its own proactivity for retention that geography alone explains
cons.example: a rural practice with no nearby alternative concluding its service is exceptional right up to the season a virtual competitor opens

failure_modes: assuming all observed retention is earned and skipping the improvements that would make it so
turning the map into a marketing script rather than a diagnostic
mapping the book once and never re-reading it as the forces shift
acceptance_tests: each named force lists at least one behaviour the practice controls and one observable signal, and a sample of clients can each be assigned a dominant force with the signal that supports it
revisit_triggers: classified exit reasons contradict the force assigned to the departing clients
a competitor changes the switching cost, for example by offering free prior-year transfer
the practice changes its service model, staffing or response-time commitment

nodes.definition: Fix the conduct rules that govern every off-season contact before a single message is drafted. No message promises, implies or compares refund size or refund speed, and no fee for any off-season line varies with a refund or with an amount recovered. No message uses audit, penalty or notice fear as a reason to buy: where urgency is real it is a statutory date stated as a date, and where it is not real it is not manufactured. Fee, scope and who performs the work are disclosed and agreed before the work starts, never presented afterwards. And a heightened-care rule applies to clients whose circumstances make pressure especially harmful - elderly clients, clients working in a second language, clients in bereavement, job loss or debt distress - under which the practice slows down, puts scope and price in writing, checks understanding rather than assuming it, and welcomes a family member or a second opinion instead of treating either as an obstacle. Off-season contact is riskier than in-season contact precisely because the client is not in a filing emergency, so any urgency in the message was manufactured by the practice.

included: the never-say list covering refund promises, comparisons and fear framing
disclosure of fee, scope and performer before agreement
heightened-care handling for vulnerable clients
the rule that urgency must be a real statutory date stated as a date
excluded: conduct during the in-season return review conversation, which the return-workflow knowledge base owns
marketing channel and creative selection
which services the credential class permits at all

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a complaint, a staff report of pressure selling, or a new content source that has not been checked against the never-say list

pros.claim: Refusing fear-selling protects the earned trust that is the entire retention asset
pros.example: a notice-support offer that explains what a notice is and what help costs, instead of warning clients that the authority is targeting people like them

cons.claim: Conduct rules cost visible short-term revenue and are hardest to hold in the thinnest month of the year
cons.example: declining a scarcity-framed planning-session push in a slow month while a competitor's version is visibly filling seats

failure_modes: fear framing arriving intact inside a vendor's newsletter template and going out unreviewed
a free review offered mainly to find something to sell
unrequested discounting under time pressure that trains the book to wait for it
arranging an elderly client's work through a relative because it is faster than speaking to the client
acceptance_tests: every off-season message and offer is checked against the never-say list before sending regardless of who wrote it, and each one names its fee, scope and performer where it asks for anything
the heightened-care rule is written with the situations it covers and the concrete handling it requires, and staff can state it without reading it
revisit_triggers: a client or staff member reports that a message felt like pressure or a threat
a new channel, vendor template or third-party content source enters the outreach mix
an off-season line is added whose natural pitch depends on urgency

nodes.definition: Draw and then police the line between what the practice may say generally in the off-season and what constitutes advice on one taxpayer's facts. Off-season contact invites exactly the questions that cross it: a recordkeeping newsletter draws a reply describing a house sale and asking what to do about it. Every inbound request is classified as general education (how a category of item is generally treated, what documents to keep, what changed for the coming season stated in general terms with the authority's own publication as the source), fact-specific work (a question that cannot be answered without the client's full picture, and therefore requires an engagement, a fee, and the return-workflow knowledge base's research and review discipline), or out of competence or credential class (referred, with the referral made plainly rather than apologetically). The habit that carries the rule is the refusal to answer a fact-specific question conversationally - in a hallway, a reply email, a social comment or a phone call taken while driving - because an off-hand answer carries the same client reliance and the same exposure as a signed return with none of the checking behind it.

included: the three-way classification of inbound off-season questions
the no-casual-answer habit across every informal channel
the conversion path from question to scoped, priced, reviewed work
the boundaries that keep general content general
excluded: the in-return ambiguity triage of research, escalate or decline, which the return-workflow knowledge base owns
the correct treatment of any actual client fact pattern
representation before an authority

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a pattern of informal answers surfaces, or a new communication channel changes how questions arrive

pros.claim: Converting fact-specific questions into engagements protects the client from an unchecked answer and the practice from unpaid exposure
pros.example: a quick question about a rental property becoming a scoped consultation with a written answer instead of a guess typed into a reply

cons.claim: Clients experience the boundary as coldness, and some route around it or leave over it
cons.example: a long-standing client who treated free answers as part of the relationship reacting badly the first time a fee is quoted for one

failure_modes: answering from memory because the question sounded simple and the client was pleasant
publishing general content that quietly walks one specific client toward a position
letting an unpriced answer chain grow across a summer until it is a full engagement nobody scoped
acceptance_tests: each inbound off-season question is recorded with its classification and, where fact-specific, the scope and fee that were sent before any substantive answer
general content carries a general-information statement with a date and the authority publication it was checked against
revisit_triggers: the same fact-specific question arrives repeatedly and should become general content
a channel is added where informal answering is the norm
a staff member is found answering fact-specific questions outside an engagement

nodes.definition: Before an off-season line is mentioned to a single client, run it through a fixed four-part filter. Authorization: does the practice's credential and registration class permit this work and any representation it implies - an obligation class that varies by jurisdiction and by credential, that changes between seasons, and that must be verified against the authority's own current publications rather than assumed from last year or copied from what other firms appear to be doing. Competence: has anyone here actually done this work well, and who reviews it when they do. Infrastructure: do the engagement letter, software, professional insurance and data-handling posture cover it. Capacity: which weeks does it consume, and what is displaced when it does. A line that fails any part is not offered, is offered only as a referral, or is deferred until the failing part is fixed, and the verdict is written down with its reason. The filter exists because off-season lines are chosen in slow months, which is precisely when the incentive to say yes to work the practice cannot properly perform is at its strongest.

included: the authorization, competence, infrastructure and capacity test applied per line
the offer, refer or defer verdict with its written reason
the requirement to verify every authorization question against current jurisdiction rules
excluded: the credential class map and initial practice registration, which the practice-setup knowledge base owns
how any approved line is then operated day to day
the pricing architecture for the line

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a credential, registration, insurance or rule change touching any offered line, or the departure of the person who carried its competence

pros.claim: One filter pass per line prevents discovering an authorization or insurance gap in the middle of a live engagement
pros.example: catching that a representation-flavoured notice engagement exceeds the practice's authorization class before any client is told help is available

cons.claim: The filter is conservative by construction and will refuse lines a bolder practice runs profitably
cons.example: deferring a bookkeeping crossover for a season because no one has been named to review the work

failure_modes: assuming last season's authorization answer still holds without re-reading the current rules
passing the competence arm because the owner once did the work years ago and nobody else can
approving a line on authorization and competence while never asking which weeks it eats
acceptance_tests: every offered line carries a dated four-part verdict, and the authorization item names the rule source consulted and the date it was checked
at least one candidate line in the portfolio has an explicit refer or defer verdict, showing the filter is capable of saying no
revisit_triggers: a credential renewal cycle, registration change or published rule change affecting any line
the person whose competence carried a line leaves or stops performing it
an insurance or engagement-letter scope change

nodes.definition: Establish what the practice may do with the client information it already holds when it wants to reach that client outside the engagement. Information collected to prepare a return is a restricted class in many jurisdictions, and using it to market a service, to offer a related product, or to pass anything to a third party is typically governed by consent-and-disclosure obligations that specify the form, the timing and the specificity of the client's permission - an obligation class to verify against the current rules of the practice's jurisdiction rather than to infer from what competitors appear to be doing. Operationally this work unit fixes the contact record itself: channel preferences per client, a working way to stop receiving the promotional class of message, the separation between service messages a client cannot opt out of (their return is ready, their notice has a deadline) and promotional messages they can, and the absolute rule that no client list is shared, sold, traded or handed to a referral partner under any commercial arrangement.

included: the consent-and-disclosure obligation class and its verify-current-rules requirement
separation of service messages from promotional messages
per-client channel preference and opt-out records
the no-sharing, no-selling rule for the client list
excluded: the technical security controls protecting taxpayer data at rest and in transit, which the return-workflow knowledge base owns
producing the content of any message
retention and destruction schedules for closed files

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a change in consent or disclosure rules, a new sending channel or tool, or a client question about how their data is used

pros.claim: Deciding permitted use once, in writing, keeps a slow-month marketing idea from becoming a disclosure problem
pros.example: declining to hand the client list to a partner offering a revenue share, because the list is never shared on any terms

cons.claim: Consent formalities slow down outreach and shrink the reachable list, sometimes sharply
cons.example: a segment-targeted educational mailing that can only go to the clients whose recorded preferences cover it

failure_modes: treating a client relationship as blanket permission for any future message
mixing a promotional offer into a service message so the client cannot opt out of it
keeping preferences in one person's memory instead of in the record
acceptance_tests: the permitted-use position is written with the obligation class named, the jurisdiction rules cited by source and date, and the review date for re-verification
every outbound message is classified service or promotional before sending, and the promotional class carries a working opt-out that is honoured in the record
revisit_triggers: consent, disclosure or communication rules in the practice's jurisdiction change or come up for renewal
a new outreach channel or third-party sending tool is introduced
a client asks how their information is being used

nodes.definition: Measure whether the book is holding, using a cohort method the practice can compute from its own records and defend to itself. Fix the denominator as the clients active in the prior season minus the states the book definition calls exits, and the numerator as those whose current-season return reached accepted transmission. Compute by entry cohort, because first-year clients behave nothing like a ten-year household and a blended figure hides both. Two corrections make the number honest. The extension lag: a rate computed at the spring deadline systematically undercounts returns that legitimately arrive months later, so every figure carries an as-of date and is recomputed after the extended deadline before any decision rests on it. The segment split: a practice can lose a large share of its simplest returns to self-preparation software while its business clients hold perfectly, and see only a mild aggregate dip that points at nothing. No outside benchmark is imported into the comparison; the only honest reference is the practice's own prior seasons on the same definitions.

included: cohort denominator and numerator construction
as-of dating and the post-extension recompute
entry-cohort and segment splits
comparison against the practice's own history only
excluded: why clients left, which the exit-reason work unit owns
deciding what to do about the number
any claim about typical or benchmark retention in the industry

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the post-extension recompute, a change in the book definition, or a segment rate that diverges from the aggregate

pros.claim: Cohort splitting exposes a first-year retention problem that a blended rate conceals completely
pros.example: seeing that clients acquired in the last three weeks of the season return far less often than clients acquired early, which points at the rushed intake rather than at price

cons.claim: Cohort slices get small quickly, and in a small book two departures swing a slice hard
cons.example: a nine-client niche cohort showing a dramatic drop that is two families moving out of the area

failure_modes: reporting a spring-deadline rate as final and acting on a number the extension tail will move
changing the definition between seasons so the trend is an artefact
quoting an industry retention figure the practice has no way to verify
acceptance_tests: every reported rate states its denominator, numerator, as-of date and the scheduled post-extension recompute date
the same season recomputed from the stored definitions reproduces the reported figure
revisit_triggers: the book definition or client states change
the post-extension recompute moves the rate materially
a segment's rate diverges from the aggregate

nodes.definition: Turn the fact that someone did not come back into evidence the practice can act on. After the season closes, work the lapsed list in a short routine that does not pester. Screen first for the non-signals - a client who died, moved away, married into another preparer's book, no longer has the filing obligation the practice serves, or was deliberately disengaged - so that unavoidable exits are not counted as failures and no bereaved family receives a win-back message. Then make one low-pressure contact to the remainder: a plain note saying they were missed, an offer to send their prior-year copies wherever they have gone, and one genuine question about what would have kept them. Classify every answer as controllable (a fee that arrived as a surprise, slow responses, an error the client noticed, a preparer change mid-book, the feeling of being processed rather than known) or not controllable (moved, a life change that removed the need, went to a relative who does it free), and route each controllable reason to the work unit that owns the cause instead of collecting reasons and admiring them.

included: lapsed-list construction and non-signal screening
the single low-pressure exit contact and its content
controllable versus uncontrollable classification
routing each controllable cause to the owning work unit
excluded: pressured win-back campaigns of any kind
computing the aggregate retention rate
fixing the in-season production defects themselves, which the return-workflow knowledge base owns

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a cluster of controllable exit reasons on one cause, or evidence that the reasons given differ from the behaviour observed before departure

pros.claim: Exit reasons name the actual defect instead of leaving the practice to guess that it was price
pros.example: three departures all mentioning an unanswered email in March, which points at response-time capacity rather than at the fee

cons.claim: Exit answers are polite and unreliable, and the reason offered is often not the reason
cons.example: clients citing cost because it is socially easier than saying they never felt the return was explained to them

failure_modes: contacting a bereaved family with a win-back message because the non-signal screen was skipped
asking so many questions that the contact becomes a survey nobody answers
collecting reasons every year and routing none of them to anyone
acceptance_tests: every lapsed client is screened for non-signals before any contact, and each contacted client receives at most one follow-up
each controllable reason recorded this season names the work unit it was routed to and what changed as a result
revisit_triggers: controllable reasons cluster on a single cause
the lapsed list grows faster than the book
the exit contact itself generates complaints

nodes.definition: Rank the book by what each client actually contributes across years, so that scarce off-season attention and scarce peak slots are allocated deliberately rather than to whoever calls loudest in February. The ranking is a mechanism, not a table of figures: for each client, set the fee the return supports against the hours the relationship truly consumes - preparation time plus document chase, mid-season scope changes, repeated explanations, post-filing questions and payment follow-up - and then adjust for payment reliability and timing, the referrals the client has actually produced, the client's fit with the segment the practice serves, and the friction the relationship creates for staff. A client paying a healthy fee whose documents arrive in three tranches two days before the deadline can contribute less than a smaller, punctual, well-organised one, and only the effort-adjusted view shows it. Two things never enter the ranking: refund size, which is not the practice's outcome to sell, and any variation in accuracy, review depth or due-diligence rigor, which stay identical across every tier. The tier is an internal allocation tool and is never disclosed to a client.

included: the effort-adjusted contribution mechanism and its components
payment behaviour, referral production and segment fit as adjustments
tier-driven allocation of off-season attention and early peak slots
excluded: setting or changing the fee itself, which the practice-setup knowledge base owns
any refund-based ranking
varying accuracy, review depth or due-diligence rigor by tier
disclosing a tier to a client

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: recorded effort or payment data that contradicts a tier, or a material change in a client's return complexity

pros.claim: Effort adjustment reveals that the largest invoice is not always the best client, which changes who gets the early slots
pros.example: a business client whose bookkeeping arrives in a carrier bag consuming triple the expected hours while a smaller, organised client is finished in one pass

cons.claim: Tiering becomes self-fulfilling when a low tier receives less attention and then leaves for exactly that reason
cons.example: a modest but loyal client who stops receiving proactive contact and departs the season a competitor calls them first

failure_modes: ranking on invoice size because effort was never recorded
letting a tier leak into how the work itself is done rather than only how attention is allocated
freezing tiers for years so a client whose situation changed is still treated as they were
acceptance_tests: each client's tier is reproducible from recorded fee, effort, payment and referral facts by someone who did not assign it
the ranking contains no refund component and no rule that changes review depth or due-diligence handling by tier
revisit_triggers: a client's return complexity or effort profile changes materially
recorded effort data becomes available where only invoices were held before
a tier assignment is contradicted by the client's actual referral or payment behaviour

nodes.definition: Use the narrow window immediately after the filing deadline - while the season's detail is still recoverable and before exhaustion erases it - to capture the facts that will otherwise be gone by autumn. Per client: which documents were missing and how late they arrived, what pushed the return onto extension, which questions the client asked twice, whether the quoted fee matched the work actually done, whether anyone had to chase payment, and any life change mentioned in passing that will change next year's return. Per practice: which weeks broke, where the queue stalled, which client behaviours produced the most rework, and which promises the practice made under pressure that it should not repeat. The window is short and it competes with the strongest urge of the practice's year, which is to stop; the only reliable defence is to schedule it as a block with a named output before the deadline arrives. Everything the off-season plan is built from - the follow-up sequence, next-year positioning, the line portfolio, the capacity blocks - is assembled out of what this window captures, and a practice that skips it spends the next season guessing at its own history.

included: the scheduled post-deadline capture block and its named output
per-client friction, fee-fit and life-change notes
per-practice bottleneck and overcommitment notes
handing those notes forward into the off-season plan
excluded: the in-season defect log and control tuning, which the return-workflow knowledge base owns
client-facing follow-up contact itself
the annual book review that happens months later

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a season in which the debrief block was skipped, or downstream work units reporting that the notes they need are missing

pros.claim: Notes taken while the season is fresh make every later off-season contact specific instead of generic
pros.example: telling a client in June exactly which two statements arrived late and what to do differently, because it was written down in April

cons.claim: The window falls exactly where the practice has the least energy, and the block is the easiest thing in the year to cancel
cons.example: a two-day debrief block quietly dropped in favour of a week off, after which nobody can reconstruct which clients caused the March jam

failure_modes: capturing only the loudest three clients and calling it a debrief
recording complaints without recording the life changes that will drive next year's work
leaving notes in individual heads or private notebooks where the follow-up sequence cannot reach them
acceptance_tests: every client filed this season has either a debrief note or an explicit nothing-to-record marker
the practice-level notes name at least the weeks that broke and the client behaviours that produced the most rework
revisit_triggers: the debrief block was skipped or truncated in any season
the follow-up sequence cannot find the specifics it needs
staffing changes so the people who hold the memory are different

nodes.definition: Convert a just-finished return into a defined starting position for the next one, in the weeks when the client still remembers the experience and is most willing to agree to a change. Positioning tells the client three things. What they will do differently: the specific statements that arrived late, the records to start keeping now, the account to organise, the mileage or expense habit to adopt in January rather than reconstruct in March. What the practice will do differently: an earlier intake date, a different appointment format, a document checklist built from their actual return rather than a generic list. And where the fee is heading and why, framed strictly on the complexity drivers of their return - a new rental, a new state, a new entity - and never on the refund they just received. Where the practice wants a structural change, such as moving a chronic late-March arrival into February or moving a paper client onto a secure portal, this is the cheapest week of the year to ask, because the friction is still fresh in the client's own memory rather than being a claim the practice has to make later against a client who has forgotten.

included: per-client instructions for next season derived from this season's friction
practice-side commitments and slot positioning
fee-direction signalling on complexity grounds only
structural change requests made while the friction is fresh
excluded: the fee schedule and pricing architecture themselves, owned by the practice-setup knowledge base
the published intake cutoff policy
executing next season's intake

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: client reactions to positioning notes, or a capacity change that invalidates a practice-side commitment already promised

pros.claim: A change agreed in the positioning window costs a fraction of the same change negotiated during peak
pros.example: moving a chronic late arriver to a February slot in May, when the client remembers the rush, rather than arguing about it in March

cons.claim: Positioning can read as blame if it is delivered as a list of the client's failures
cons.example: a note itemising every late document that leaves a good client feeling scolded rather than helped

failure_modes: sending the same generic note to the whole book so nothing in it is actionable
signalling a fee direction while pointing at the refund the client just received
promising a practice-side change the capacity plan has not agreed to
acceptance_tests: each retained client's note names what they do differently, what the practice does differently, and any fee direction with the complexity driver behind it
no positioning note references refund size, refund speed or a comparison with another preparer's outcome
revisit_triggers: the capacity plan changes and a promised practice-side commitment can no longer be met
clients respond to positioning notes as criticism
the fee direction signalled diverges from what intake actually quotes

nodes.definition: Design the rhythm of contact between the delivered return and the next season's intake so the practice stays present without becoming noise. The sequence contains a small number of contacts, each with a real reason to exist: the delivery-and-close message carrying copies, what to keep and for how long as a general matter; a mid-year note that is genuinely useful to that client's class rather than a generic newsletter forwarded to everyone; a statutory-date reminder sent only to the clients who actually have one, such as extension filers and estimate payers, stated as a date rather than a warning; and the pre-season note that opens intake with a specific slot. Each contact carries one ask at most, names who it is from, and gives the promotional class an easy way to stop. The restraint is the design rather than a limitation of it: a practice that mails its whole book every month teaches the book to ignore its mail, and then the one message that genuinely mattered arrives inside a stream nobody opens any more.

included: the contact rhythm and the reason each contact exists
segmentation so a message goes only to the class it is relevant to
the one-ask rule and sender identification
opt-out handling for the promotional class
excluded: whether contact is permitted at all, which the consent and permitted-use work unit decides
content that crosses into advice on a client's facts
outreach to people who are not clients

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: rising opt-outs or complaints on a contact, or debrief evidence that clients lacked information the sequence should have carried

pros.claim: A short, relevant sequence keeps the practice in mind while preserving the attention needed for the messages that matter
pros.example: an estimate-date reminder that is opened because it is one of only four messages that client received all year

cons.claim: Restraint means the practice is invisible for long stretches, and a competitor contacting monthly may reach the client first
cons.example: a client who books elsewhere in January because the other firm's reminder arrived two weeks before the practice's pre-season note

failure_modes: sending a generic newsletter to the whole book because segmentation is work
stacking several asks into one message so none of them lands
letting a vendor's automated sequence run at a cadence nobody chose
acceptance_tests: each contact in the sequence has a stated reason, a defined recipient class and at most one ask
statutory-date reminders reach only clients who actually have that date and state it as a date with no warning framing
revisit_triggers: opt-out or complaint volume rises on any contact
the debrief notes show clients missing information the sequence should have carried
a new off-season line changes what the book needs to hear

nodes.definition: Decide which clients the practice will not carry into the next season, and end those relationships cleanly and early. The grounds are practice grounds and are written down: repeated pressure to take positions the practice will not sign or to leave documented income off a return; refusal to supply the substantiation that a claimed credit or filing status requires, which is a compliance class the practice does not negotiate; arrival so consistently late that the client's return can only be produced at a quality the practice will not defend; abuse of staff; and structural fee mismatch where the effort has drifted far past anything the client will pay. Execution matters as much as the decision. Notify well before the next season rather than at the door, put it in writing without accusation or diagnosis, offer copies of prior-year documents and workpapers the client is entitled to, and never leave a client believing they still have a preparer when they do not. Handled this way, disengagement is a retention instrument in the honest sense: it returns capacity and standards to the clients the practice intends to keep.

included: the written practice-standard grounds
timing and written notification well before intake
prior-document and workpaper handover
the capacity and standards rationale for doing it at all
excluded: declining a single ambiguous item or a single return inside a season, which the return-workflow knowledge base owns
any ground unrelated to practice standards
the ranking exercise that surfaces candidates

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a recurring ground across many clients pointing at a practice-side cause, or a listed client's behaviour changing before notification

pros.claim: Removing a standards-violating relationship protects the signature the whole practice depends on
pros.example: ending a relationship with a client who each year presses for an unsupported deduction, rather than re-fighting it under deadline pressure

cons.claim: Disengagement removes revenue immediately and the freed capacity is only worth something if it is deliberately reallocated
cons.example: dropping several difficult clients in a season when the growth room they vacate is never filled

failure_modes: telling the client only when they arrive at the door in February
writing a notice that diagnoses the client's character rather than stating the practice's decision
withholding prior-year documents the client is entitled to
disengaging the difficult clients while keeping the one whose pressure is the actual standards risk
acceptance_tests: every disengagement names a written practice-standard ground, a notification date that precedes the next intake opening, and a completed document handover offer
the notice contains no accusation and no reference to any ground outside the written list
revisit_triggers: a client on the list changes the behaviour that caused it
the same ground recurs across many clients, indicating a practice-side cause
capacity freed by disengagement is not reallocated in the growth plan

nodes.definition: Treat the returns that went on extension as a named book with its own calendar rather than as leftovers that will get done eventually. The list lives outside anyone's head and carries, per client, what is still missing, who owes the next action, when that action is due, and the extended statutory date that governs the return - a date and a set of obligations that are jurisdiction-specific, change between seasons, and must be read from the authority's own current publications rather than recalled. The work is sequenced in waves through the quiet months so the population empties steadily instead of recreating a second crunch in the final fortnight. Client communication is part of the book: extension clients are told plainly what an extension does and does not do, in particular that an extension of time to file and any obligation to pay are separate matters whose current requirements they must confirm for their own jurisdiction. And each extension carries a conversion question - was the cause structural, such as a partnership statement that simply arrives when it arrives, or behavioural, such as documents gathered slowly - because only the behavioural ones can be positioned back into the main season next year.

included: the tracked extension list with per-client next action, owner and governing date
wave sequencing across the quiet months
the client-facing explanation of what an extension is
structural versus behavioural cause classification and conversion
excluded: the in-season decision to extend a return for quality reasons, which the return-workflow knowledge base owns
the current statutory dates, payment obligations or penalty consequences themselves
preparing the return

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: growth in the extension population, a crunch shape at the extended deadline, or a change in the jurisdiction's published extension rules

pros.claim: A tracked, wave-sequenced book turns the extension population from a looming cliff into steady summer revenue
pros.example: clearing the extension list in monthly waves so the final weeks hold only the returns genuinely waiting on third-party statements

cons.claim: The book demands administrative discipline in the months when the practice least wants any, and it decays quickly if the list is not maintained
cons.example: a list last updated in May that by August no longer matches who is actually waiting on what

failure_modes: holding the extension population in memory and rediscovering it weeks before the extended deadline
letting clients believe an extension postpones every obligation rather than the filing itself
working the easy extensions first so the hardest returns land in the final fortnight
never asking why each return went on extension, so the same clients extend every year
acceptance_tests: every extension client appears on the shared list with a next action, an owner and the governing date recorded outside anyone's memory
each extension carries a structural or behavioural cause classification, and the behavioural ones appear in the positioning notes for next season
revisit_triggers: the extension population grows season over season
extended-deadline weeks show a crunch shape resembling the spring peak
published extension rules or dates for the practice's jurisdiction change

nodes.definition: Offer amendment work as an off-season line, strictly for situations that originate outside the practice's own production: a client whose corrected statement arrived after the return was filed, a client who finds an item they never claimed on a year prepared somewhere else, a new client arriving with a prior-preparer return that contains a defect. Running it as a line rather than as favours means scoping each amendment as its own engagement with its own written scope, its own fee and its own review, because an amendment is a full re-examination of a filed position and carries at least the diligence the original required. It means qualifying honestly, including telling a client plainly when an amendment is not worth doing or when the case for it is too thin to sign. And it means refusing the marketing that makes this line dangerous: the free-review-to-find-money pitch that promises an outcome before any facts are known, and any fee that scales with what is recovered. Amendments caused by the practice's own error are categorically not this line - they are remediation governed by the return-workflow knowledge base, handled under that discipline, and never repriced as new revenue.

included: externally-originated amendment engagements
per-amendment written scope, fee and review
honest qualification including advising against an amendment
the prohibition on outcome-promising review offers and recovery-linked fees
excluded: correcting the practice's own filing errors, which is remediation under the return-workflow knowledge base and is never billed as a new line
determining the correct treatment of the underlying item
representation in any resulting authority interaction beyond the credential class

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a rise in amendments tracing to the practice's own work, or pressure to run an outcome-promising review campaign

pros.claim: Scoping each amendment as its own engagement keeps a re-examination from being done at favour speed with favour care
pros.example: a prior-preparer defect handled with a written scope and a second review rather than as a quick fix squeezed between other work

cons.claim: The line's honest version converts far worse than the pitch the practice is forbidden to use
cons.example: declining a free-review campaign that promises to find missed money, and watching a less scrupulous competitor fill their summer with it

failure_modes: amending on a client's assertion without the substantiation the position needs
quoting an amendment before checking whether the original was the practice's own work
pricing the engagement as a share of what is recovered
treating an amendment as a lighter job than an original return
acceptance_tests: every amendment engagement records the origin of the underlying error, a written scope and fee agreed before work, and a review at least equal to an original return
no amendment offer, message or conversation states or implies an expected recovery, and no fee varies with the amount recovered
revisit_triggers: amendments trace back to the practice's own work more often than expected
the qualification step is being skipped under volume pressure
a marketing template for the line arrives from a vendor

nodes.definition: Define how the practice helps a client who receives correspondence from a tax authority outside the season, and exactly where that help stops. The service is: read the notice with the client, identify what it actually asks and by when, retrieve the workpapers and substantiation already on file, and either prepare the documented response the client sends or explain that the matter requires representation the practice's credential class does not permit and refer it onward. Scope, fee and the response deadline go in writing before work begins, and the client is told plainly that no outcome can be promised, only a documented and timely response. Two disciplines keep this line from becoming a liability. First, the clock is external: a notice carries a real date, so intake for this line runs same-week rather than queuing behind project work, and the date is read from the notice and the authority's current publications rather than assumed. Second, the practice checks its own file before quoting anything, because a notice that traces to the practice's own error moves immediately into the return-workflow knowledge base's disclosure and correction path instead of being billed as support.

included: notice triage, deadline identification and file retrieval
documented response support within the credential class
written scope, fee and deadline before work, with no outcome promise
same-week intake and the check-my-own-file-first rule
excluded: representation before an authority beyond what the credential class permits, a class the practice-setup knowledge base defines
any promise or prediction about how a notice will be resolved
the practice's own-error disclosure path

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a change in notice volume or type, or a change in the representation rules governing the practice's credential class

pros.claim: A defined notice service turns the most frightening moment a client has all year into the strongest evidence that the practice is worth keeping
pros.example: a client who receives a notice in August, gets a same-week reading of what it asks and by when, and tells three people about it

cons.claim: The line arrives unpredictably with an external deadline and disrupts whatever block it lands in
cons.example: three notices in one week displacing planned educational work because their response dates cannot move

failure_modes: queueing a notice behind project work until the response window is nearly gone
quoting a support fee for a matter caused by the practice's own error
drifting into representation the credential class does not permit because the client asked and the situation was urgent
reassuring a frightened client with an outcome prediction
acceptance_tests: every notice engagement records the response deadline taken from the notice, a same-week first contact, and a written scope and fee agreed before work
each engagement records the own-file check and its result, and no engagement letter or conversation contains an outcome promise
revisit_triggers: notice volume changes materially or clusters on one return type
the credential class or representation rules change
a notice arrives that the practice cannot answer within its authorization

nodes.definition: Run periodic estimated-payment support for the clients whose situation involves it - business owners, the newly self-employed, clients with substantial income that is not subject to withholding - as a scheduled recurring service rather than as ad-hoc favours answered from memory. The operating shape is a per-cycle loop: request the period's figures on a fixed date, produce the computation the client needs, deliver it with the payment mechanics for their jurisdiction, and record what was sent and when. The applicable dates, thresholds and safe-harbour-style provisions are jurisdiction- and year-specific and are read from the authority's current publications each cycle rather than carried forward from last year's memory. The line earns its place for three reasons at once: it produces revenue in months that otherwise produce none, it creates several natural contact points a year with exactly the clients whose returns are the most complex, and it surfaces the mid-year business and life changes that would otherwise ambush the practice at intake. Its real cost is structural: it converts a seasonal calendar into a year-round one with dates the practice cannot miss.

included: the per-cycle request, compute, deliver and record loop
which clients the line is offered to and why
the current-rules verification performed each cycle
the contact-point and early-warning value of the line
excluded: personalized planning advice on how a client should structure income, entities or payments
the underlying computation rules themselves
any assertion of specific dates, thresholds or safe-harbour parameters

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a change in the jurisdiction's estimate dates or mechanics, or a missed cycle in the practice's own record

pros.claim: Several dated touchpoints a year with the most complex clients surface changes long before intake
pros.example: learning in a mid-year cycle that a client opened a second location in another state, months before that becomes an intake surprise

cons.claim: The line binds the practice to external dates it cannot move, in the months it wanted for recovery and preparation
cons.example: a cycle date landing inside the pre-season block and displacing software and training preparation

failure_modes: carrying last year's dates and thresholds forward instead of re-reading the current publications
letting the loop become informal so a cycle passes with no record of what was sent
drifting from computation support into structuring advice the engagement never scoped
offering the line to clients whose situation does not actually involve it
acceptance_tests: each cycle records the date the current rules were checked, the figures requested, what was delivered and when
the client list for the line is derived from situation criteria rather than from who asked, and each engagement states that it is computation support rather than planning advice
revisit_triggers: the jurisdiction changes estimate dates, thresholds or payment mechanics
a cycle is missed or delivered late for any client
clients begin asking structuring questions the engagement does not cover

nodes.definition: Package what the practice knows into general educational offers that raise a client's competence without becoming advice on their situation: a recordkeeping guide written for the segment the practice actually serves, a short session on what changes for the coming season stated in general terms with the authority's own publication named as the source, a document-organisation walkthrough for people who have just started a business, a mid-year explainer on what to bring and why it is asked for. Every piece carries a general-information statement, a date, and the publication it was checked against, and every piece is re-checked before reuse because tax content decays between seasons and a stale guide is worse than none. The offer is genuinely valuable to the client, and it is useful to the practice for a second reason that should be stated plainly rather than hidden: educated clients arrive with better documents, which lowers the effort each return consumes, and the education itself is the most reproducible demonstration of the proactivity that the retention mechanism depends on.

included: general educational content and sessions built for the served segment
the general-information statement, the date and the source publication on every piece
re-verification before any reuse
the effort-reduction and demonstrated-proactivity payoff
excluded: individualized planning recommendations of any kind
content that walks a specific client toward a specific position
classifying inbound fact-specific questions, which the education-versus-advice work unit owns

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a published rule change touching existing content, or a recurring fact-specific question generated by a piece

pros.claim: General education is the cheapest reproducible source of the proactivity that keeps clients
pros.example: a recordkeeping session in autumn that a client remembers in March when their organised receipts cut an hour from their return

cons.claim: Content decays between seasons and republished material can be wrong in ways clients rely on
cons.example: a guide reused from a prior season describing a treatment the current published rules no longer support

failure_modes: reusing last season's material without re-checking it against current publications
letting a session drift into answering one attendee's specific facts in front of the room
producing content for a general audience rather than for the segment the practice serves
omitting the general-information statement so the piece reads as advice
acceptance_tests: every published piece carries a general-information statement, a date and the source publication it was checked against, with a re-check date before reuse
sessions have a stated rule for redirecting individual fact-specific questions into a scoped engagement, and it is used when one arises
revisit_triggers: published rules change on any topic the content covers
the same fact-specific question keeps arising from a piece
the practice changes the segment it serves

nodes.definition: Decide whether to take on periodic bookkeeping or write-up work for the practice's small-business clients, and if so on what terms. The pull is strong and genuine: the work recurs monthly rather than seasonally, it converts a carrier-bag client into a clean-books client whose return costs far less to produce and can be started earlier, and it deepens the relationships that already sit at the top of the book. The pushback is equally real and is usually underweighted in the slow month when the decision gets made: bookkeeping is a different competence with its own errors and its own review needs, it draws capacity from exactly the months the practice needs for recovery and preparation, its deliverables carry their own recurring deadlines that do not pause for the filing season, and a practice that prepares the books and then prepares the return from them has quietly lost the outside perspective it had when the numbers arrived from somewhere else. The decision is taken per client class rather than per persuasive client, and it is not taken at all without naming who performs the work during peak weeks.

included: the crossover decision and the terms it is accepted on
the return-cost and relationship-depth benefits
the competence, capacity, recurring-deadline and lost-perspective costs
naming the performer and the coverage plan for peak weeks
excluded: how bookkeeping work is actually performed and its own quality controls
accounting or software instruction delivered to clients
attest or audit engagements of any kind

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the monthly load approaching the working block's capacity, or a change in who performs and reviews the work

pros.claim: Clean books produced through the year make the client's return cheaper to prepare and possible to start early
pros.example: a business client whose reconciled year-end figures arrive in January instead of a box of receipts in March

cons.claim: The line carries monthly deadlines into the months the practice needs for recovery and preparation, and it is hard to exit once clients depend on it
cons.example: a monthly close falling in the first peak week with no named alternate performer

failure_modes: accepting the line client by client until the monthly load is larger than anyone decided
leaving peak-season coverage unstated until the first peak week arrives
reviewing the return against books the same person produced, with no outside check
assuming preparation competence transfers to bookkeeping competence
acceptance_tests: the decision is recorded per client class with the named performer, the review arrangement and the written peak-season coverage plan
each crossover engagement states what happens to its monthly deliverable during the peak block, agreed before the first close
revisit_triggers: the monthly load approaches the working block's capacity
the person performing the work changes or leaves
a return is found to have been reviewed only against books the same person produced

nodes.definition: Lay the whole year out as a small number of named blocks and assign every off-season commitment to one of them, so the practice stops selling work in months it has already spent. The blocks are: peak, which is untouchable; a genuine recovery block immediately after the deadline, protected because an exhausted preparer produces exactly the error classes the return-workflow knowledge base exists to prevent; the working off-season, which carries the extension waves, the estimate cycles, notice work, educational offers and any bookkeeping crossover; and a pre-season block for software setup, training, credential renewal, client communications and staffing, protected just as hard because everything deferred out of it reappears as chaos in the first peak week. Smoothing means matching commitments to the working block's real capacity, in weeks, and refusing, capping or rescheduling anything that would spill into a protected block. The plan is also where externally dated obligations - extension deadlines, estimate cycles, notice response dates - are placed first, because they cannot move and everything discretionary must be arranged around them.

included: the named year blocks and the rules protecting each
assignment of every off-season commitment to a block in weeks
the refusal, cap or reschedule rule when a commitment spills into a protected block
placing externally dated obligations before discretionary work
excluded: peak-week throughput modelling and the published intake cutoff, which the practice-setup knowledge base owns
scheduling the internal production of a single return
hiring and staffing decisions themselves

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an overrun against assigned weeks, a breached protected block, or a new dated obligation entering the year

pros.claim: Assigning commitments to named blocks makes overcommitment visible in advance rather than in the week it detonates
pros.example: seeing at the point of sale that a new monthly line would consume the pre-season block, and capping it before agreeing

cons.claim: Protected blocks refuse revenue that is genuinely available, and the refusal is hardest to justify in the quietest month
cons.example: turning down a summer engagement that would have paid well because it would have consumed the recovery block

failure_modes: treating the recovery block as slack to be spent rather than as capacity that protects the peak
planning in months rather than weeks so two commitments quietly occupy the same fortnight
placing discretionary work before externally dated obligations
letting the pre-season block erode until the first peak week absorbs the deferred setup
acceptance_tests: every accepted off-season commitment names its block and its weeks, and no commitment sits in the recovery or pre-season block
externally dated obligations for the coming year are placed in the plan before any discretionary work is scheduled
revisit_triggers: a line overruns its assigned weeks
a protected block is breached in any season
a new line, staff change or externally dated obligation enters the year

nodes.definition: Understand, and then deliberately serve, the mechanism that actually produces referrals in this business. A client refers when they have just experienced something specific enough to repeat in one sentence to someone whose situation resembles their own - the practice caught something the last preparer had missed, the answer came back the same day, the fee was exactly what was quoted - and when the opportunity to mention it arrives near that experience rather than in a campaign months later. The practical work is therefore to identify which referrable moments the practice genuinely creates, to ask once and plainly at the point of a satisfied delivery, to make acting on it easy for the person referring, and to record where every new client came from so the mechanism is measured rather than assumed. Two hard boundaries apply. Nothing of value is offered in exchange for a referral until it has been checked whether compensated referral arrangements are permitted for the practice's credential class and jurisdiction, which is an obligation class to verify against current published rules. And no client is ever chased, incentivised into awkwardness, or allowed to feel that the relationship depends on producing names.

included: the referrable-moment mechanism and which moments the practice creates
the single plain ask at delivery
source recording for every new client
the permitted-arrangement check and the no-pressure rule
excluded: paid advertising, channel strategy and creative production
the practice's overall acquisition plan
any claim about typical referral rates or acquisition costs

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a change in compensated-referral rules, or recorded source data showing referral flow concentrating or producing poor-fit clients

pros.claim: Asking at the referrable moment costs nothing and reaches people whose situation already matches the practice's competence
pros.example: a business owner who has just been walked through a clean result mentioning it to two peers in the same trade that month

cons.claim: Referral flow is lumpy and arrives on its own schedule, often when the season's capacity is already committed
cons.example: a wave of referrals from one delighted client landing in the final weeks when no slots remain

failure_modes: asking the whole book in a campaign instead of asking one client at their own moment
offering an inducement before checking whether compensated arrangements are permitted
never recording where new clients came from, so the mechanism cannot be read a year later
repeating the ask until a good client starts avoiding the practice's messages
acceptance_tests: every new client record contains a source, captured at intake rather than reconstructed later
any inducement or arrangement offered for referrals is documented with the permitted-arrangement check, its rule source and the date it was verified
revisit_triggers: referral sources concentrate in one client or one segment
compensated-referral rules for the credential class change
new clients arrive whose fit with the served segment is poor

nodes.definition: Decide how much new business the book can absorb in a season and in what order the remaining slots are filled, starting from the fact that the returning base has the first claim on capacity. The reasoning runs in one direction: take peak capacity as the practice-setup knowledge base defines it, subtract the returning base's expected demand at its historical arrival shape, and treat what is left as the season's genuine growth room. Then fill that room deliberately - favouring the return classes the practice is fastest and safest at, the segments it has committed to serve, and the referral sources that have historically produced good-fit clients - rather than filling it with whoever happens to appear in the final three weeks. Growth taken beyond that room is never free: it is paid for out of response times, review depth and the felt experience that holds the existing book, which is why an aggressive growth season is so often followed by a retention drop that nobody connects back to it. Where demand genuinely exceeds the room, the honest answers are a dated slot next season or a referral elsewhere, not acceptance.

included: the capacity-minus-returning-demand derivation of growth room
slot allocation priority and fit-based selection
the delayed retention cost of exceeding the room
the dated-slot and referral-out answers when demand exceeds it
excluded: the peak capacity model and the published intake cutoff, which the practice-setup knowledge base owns
marketing execution and channel spend
the per-return acceptance screening of an individual new client

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: actual returning demand diverging from the estimate used, or a retention drop in the season following a growth push

pros.claim: Deriving the room before intake opens converts a season of ad-hoc yeses into a decision made once, calmly
pros.example: knowing in December how many new returns the season can hold, so the third week of March is not the moment that question is answered

cons.claim: The computed room rests on an expected returning demand that is itself an estimate, and a wrong estimate either wastes capacity or oversells it
cons.example: reserving for a returning base that turns out smaller than expected, leaving the practice underfilled in a season it turned work away

failure_modes: measuring growth by count of new clients while the existing book's service quietly degrades
filling the room with whoever arrives last because no allocation priority was set
treating a referral wave as free capacity
never comparing the next season's retention against the growth taken this one
